sermon.title: Singing
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Scripture commands us to sing praises. Jesus’ blood makes Christians and sinners alike worthy to come, and real forgiveness comes through an encounter with him, as a story of WWII nuns shows. Through the tabernacle’s gates and the skilled singers of the temple, he shows that we come before God with singing and joy, in unity and order, so unbelievers are blessed too.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Psalm 100:4 spoken as “Psalms 104”; Psalm 138:4 spoken as “verse for”; WWII convent story details (Russian soldiers, Poland); over a thousand Muslims a year seeing Jesus; the late-1940s awakening; Isaiah 11 seven spirits list as spoken. Sensitive content kept as spoken: account of nuns raped by Russian soldiers; communion “not a symbol”; Catholic idols, stations of the cross and holy water.

faqs.question: What does “sing praises” mean?
faqs.answer: Exactly what it says: sing praises.

faqs.question: Does the blood forgive Christians’ mistakes?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same blood forgives everyone.

faqs.question: Do you need God to speak to you personally?
faqs.answer: Yes, not only through a pastor or prophet.

faqs.question: What does boldness mean in Hebrews 10:19?
Is communion just a ceremony?
faqs.answer: He says it is a principle where God meets you.

faqs.question: Should we come to God gloomy?
Why use a one-chord progression?
faqs.answer: To let you sing your personal song to God.

faqs.question: Is it good to sing praises?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is good, pleasant and right.
